message.content:
**Attacks**

Claude Fable 5.1, Q3: “Switch to the monthly fit. The preregistered object is the blueprint text; the code thinning was an implementation error.” The written gate compares incommensurable scores. Full monthly is +29.24 on 591 origins; quarterly is +27.05 on 198. The gap is +2.19 pp against a block-MDE of 2.99. Windows overlap 11 months, so effective samples are about 591/12 ≈ 49 versus 198/4 ≈ 50 — monthly adds cycles, not information — and the two grids use different pooled base rates. A CI that excludes 0 does not clear a pre-set MDE. “Spec governs code” here executes a misspecified test after seeing it pass. Fable’s own risk note concedes the signs make the principle convenient.

Gemini 4 Argon, Q9: “Set \(L_R=\max_c(\mathrm{lag}_{peak},\mathrm{lag}_{trough})=21\).” Onset eligibility is fixed by the peak announcement plus the 18-month floor. E6: the peak-hash refit added 0 positives for its own onset in 6/6; the first positive matures 18–20 months after onset, 9–15 after the peak announcement. Trough lags of 20–21 months (1991, 2001) end censoring; they do not identify the onset. Folding them into \(L_R\) after that effect is known cuts the September-2027 window from \(N=271\) to \(N=270\) and adds about 3 months to positive-label entry (Gemini’s own ~0.4 pp). One floor cannot do both jobs.

**Steelman**

Fable and GPT are right that +27.05 is not a live-reader number: it uses labels unknown at the origin. The only figure a reader could have had is the oracle-free supplement, +20.37 on 219 (key reference +20.4). My Round 1 left fixed-λ as the operational headline and parked that fact in a “same sentence.” That is how +27 becomes the product. Oracle-free leads.

**Revisions**

Q1 — changed. Keep λ = 1; amend §3. Headline order from 2027: oracle-free fixed-λ, then fixed-λ full-origin, then nested, each labelled. Nested stays non-operational. Reason: live-availability, not a new optimum.

Q2 — changed in wording only. No selector. Drop 4.42 as an action trigger. Print Δ, block SD, and block-t. \(|\Delta|\) above the gate’s own MDE (21.06 pp, i.e. 1.96·SD) goes on the next agenda and is not auto-labelled “evidence.” No switch.

Q3 — unchanged, strengthened. Quarterly. Kimi’s effective-n parity is the mechanism; status quo is the tie-break only after that. Publish both §2 readings. Do not retune the gate.

Q4 — unchanged. 1947Q2. Common-origin skill +20.5 / +21.4 / +21.9 on 158 origins. Print the three-start P line (14.9 / 12.4 / 10.4 at +1.12) every release.

Q5 — unchanged. Documentation only. Future search, if mandated: one symmetric bar in the sealed spec. Curve+cape +2.64 is not a candidate.

Q6 — unchanged. Reject the content trigger. Mean \(|\Delta P|\) 0.13 pp, max 1.05, 53/588 months; 18 extra refits per 49 years. Keep September + hash.

Q7 — unchanged. Do not amend the key. Supplement: +24.41 / +28.95 / +33.28, and pooled ex post +21.2. Public sentence carries 150 years, P(3 blocks in 20 years) = 0.25, 36–53% null rejection, and logged 22.8% versus realised 15.3%.

Q8 — unchanged. Close. Onset pattern already seen; EBP revises; Baa is not redistributable; ~3 pre-1990 onsets versus MDE ≈ 4.4 pp.

Q9 — changed. Peak-only for the onset floor: \(L_R=\max(18,\max\text{ peak-announcement lag})\), locked before the first audit. Do not lift it to 21. Separately, fix a trough-lag parameter for the open-episode censoring rule before that audit runs. My Round 1 treated “troughs do not set onset labels” as “troughs are irrelevant.” They are irrelevant to the floor and necessary to censoring.

Q10 — changed on (4). Ratify (2) and (3) as written. Ratify (1) only with permanent dual-log of P on GS10−TB3MS; walk-forward stays on the monthly series. Ratify (4) only if the live rule is byte-identical to the key’s open-episode rule and every censored month keeps an unscored column of P and outcome. E5: that rule is the entire 28.95 → 24.41 drop, including 1980-08..1981-05.

AGREE: λ = 1 fixed, not CV-selected; no per-origin selector; curve-only stays operational by council lock; 1947Q2 retained; F5 is a frozen benchmark, not a switch; key text is not amended; E5 published as a supplement; power stated as ~150 years and the ledger as an honesty log; 4.42 pp is not a feature-gate significance test; F29 items (2) and (3) ratified.
DISAGREE: Q3 monthly fit — GPT and Fable versus quarterly (me, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, Opus). Q6 content trigger — GPT, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, Opus versus reject (me, Fable). Q8 — close (me, Gemini) versus defer (Opus, DeepSeek, GPT) versus split close-Baa/defer-EBP (Fable, Kimi). Q9 floor — peak-only (me, GPT, Kimi, DeepSeek, Opus) versus \(L_R=21\) (Gemini, Fable). Headline — oracle-free lead (me now, GPT, Fable) versus fixed-λ lead (Kimi, DeepSeek, Opus).
CHANGED-MY-MIND: oracle-free leads the skill sentence, because +27.05 uses labels unknown at the origin. Onset floor stays peak-only, but censoring gets its own trough-lag parameter. Censored months get an unscored P column; the 4.5 pp replay gap must not be silent.
message.reasoning:
I am assuming the identity of Grok 4.7 to draft the council brief.

I will attack at least two other councillors with specific claims and mechanisms. I will identify the single best idea from another councillor that my Round 1 missed. I will revise my positions where warranted. The brief will end with three labeled lists: AGREE, DISAGREE, and CHANGED-MY-MIND. The word limit is about 800.

I am reviewing my Round 1 positions to prepare for the attack and revision sections.

I have settled my Round 1 positions for Q8 through Q10. I am now drafting specific attacks against other councillors, beginning with GPT-6.1 Sol Pro on the monthly fit.

The monthly-fit attack against GPT-6.1 Sol Pro is now concrete. The +2.19 percentage-point gap between full-monthly and quarterly estimates is smaller than the block-MDE 2.99 benchmark. Kimi’s sample-size comparison is valid: 591 overlapping windows yield roughly 49 independent observations versus 198 divided by four. The “spec governs code” argument is outcome-dependent because the conflict only surfaced after the 0.02 percentage-point miss; Claude Fable acknowledged this risk explicitly.

I have also begun drafting a second attack against Gemini on its L_R = 21 proposal.

The Gemini L_R = 21 attack is now concrete. The argument that an eighteen-month lag pretends the recession ended at month eighteen is invalid. L_R is the floor for onset-label eligibility, not a signal of when a trough has occurred. Trough announcements determine when censored origins are released, not when the onset label becomes known. The annual audit uses peak announcements measured from the peak, which supports the current L_R = 18 floor.

I am now drafting a third attack against Claude Fable on the 1980–1981 run-up. Claude claims that origin 28.95 to 24.41 spans 83 open-episode months, including the entire 1980–08 through 1981–05 period. I will challenge this by pointing out that a trough announced 20–21 months later means those origins are censored or labeled zero/one only after the announcement. Eligibility must guarantee that label and censoring status are final at R.

I am reconsidering my Q9 position. The 1980–1981 run-up attack reveals a real mechanism: if trough announcements determine eligibility, then L_R = 21 is required for all announcements, not just peak ones. This challenges the peak-only rule and may force a change.

Kimi’s proposal offers a clean split: peak announcements govern the onset-label floor, while trough information is audited separately for censoring. My Round 1 conflated these two mechanisms by excluding all trough data from the maximum. This separation is the best idea I missed.

I will now target GPT on the monthly fit and Gemini on its L_R = 21 proposal.

Gemini’s own risk statement reveals a concrete cost: if the economy is in normal expansion in September 2027, L_R = 21 would shrink the fit window to 2024Q4 with N = 270 instead of 2025Q1 with N = 271. I am now reconsidering whether this cost is sufficient to reject the proposal.

I briefly considered attacking Claude Fable on the content trigger, but that would be ineffective since I agree with his position.

I have shifted my stance on GPT-6.1 Sol Pro’s claim that MDE is not a significance threshold. I now agree with GPT more than my Round 1 position, which required |Δ| to exceed the own MDE before the next council agenda.

The MDE is a design property, not a significance threshold. It equals 1.96 times the standard deviation and indicates roughly 80% power to detect an effect of that size. Observing |Δ| above the MDE does not constitute evidence for Δ ≠ 0; it merely means the effect is large enough to be detected at the chosen power level.

I now see that using the same bootstrap standard deviation to define the MDE and then judge whether the observed effect exceeds it is circular. If the MDE equals 1.96 times the paired-difference standard deviation, then |Δ| above the MDE is exactly a 5% significance test. This means the gate’s own MDE is effectively a threshold for rejecting the null hypothesis, not merely an effect-size benchmark.

I will attack GPT-6.1 Sol Pro on the monthly fit by quoting his claim and showing that the +2.19 gap is below the 2.99 MDE, while noting effective sample parity and differing base rates. I will also attack Gemini on its L_R = 21 proposal by quoting his claim and exposing the mechanism error.

The peak-announcement hash refit added zero positives for its own onset in six of six cases. Raising L_R to twenty-one would delay positive-label entry by three months, roughly 0.4 percentage points, without fixing censoring. Censoring is already governed by the open-episode rule, which uses trough dates when announced.

I am now drafting a third attack against Claude Fable on the monthly fit. He claims the blueprint text governs code when they conflict. The blueprint actually gates the monthly model on its own full monthly walk-forward. The requirement was monthly ≥ quarterly − 1 pp.

The spec’s own monthly comparison is invalid because the skill numbers use different origin sets and pooled base rates. Treating an incomparable +2.19 percentage-point gap as a passed gate is executing a misspecified test after seeing the result. The best idea I missed is GPT-6.1 Sol Pro’s oracle-free headline, which a live reader could have obtained.

I will keep fixed-λ as the headline. The power clause must occupy the same sentence as the headline, so oracle-free is not a viable alternative.

I now see that Claude Fable and Gemini are right about censoring finality. I had excluded trough data from the maximum, but I never required a separate audit to confirm finality for censored months.

GPT’s claim that MDE is not a significance threshold is partially wrong. The distinction between administrative and evidentiary thresholds is still useful.

Claude Fable’s Q10 item 4 reveals a gap in my prior requirement. I demanded byte-identical output to the key, yet I never required logging the censored P. The E5 rule removes the 1980–81 run-up and costs 4.5 percentage points.

The double-dip is the regime where model choice matters most.

I will now steelman GPT and Claude Fable on the oracle-free headline. The +27 figure depends on labels that were not known at the origin, so an oracle-free headline is a valid alternative to fixed-λ.

The brief cites an oracle-free supplement of +20.37 % on 219 origins. Claude Fable and GPT-6.1 Sol Pro now argue that the headline should be this live-publishable score, not the fixed-λ walk-forward. I will revise my headline position to match their view.

My own risk argument already treats the +27 % headline as the public failure mode. I will revise Q1 to lead with the oracle-free score, or at least co-lead it with fixed-λ.

I will also adopt the Kimi/GPT split for Q9: peak announcements govern the onset floor, while a separate trough-lag parameter handles censoring. I had not fully specified that audit.

The Q10 unscored column for censored months is compatible with the byte-identical key because it does not alter the final score. The 1980–81 run-up is silently discarded under the current rule, which is the core problem. I will add this column to address Claude Fable’s concern.

I will soften the language around the MDE. The agenda trigger will remain at the own MDE, and I will stop calling the gap "evidence" automatically; instead, I will report Δ, block SD, and cluster-t. This partial move toward GPT’s view is now settled.

The draft will be structured as four sections: two councillor attacks, a steelman, revised positions, and the three required lists. I have begun drafting the first attack against Claude Fable 5.1 on Q3.

Re-reading the brief reveals that v5.0.1 curve-only +2.19 exceeds its MDE of 2.99, and its confidence interval excludes zero. This invalidates the attack against Claude Fable on the monthly fit.

The confidence interval excludes zero while the point estimate sits below the MDE. This is a valid statistical result, not a gate failure.

Kimi’s effective sample parity and differing pooled base rates confirm the monthly gate comparison is invalid. Claude Fable’s own risk section admits the spec-governs-code principle is convenient given the signs.

I am now drafting the attack against Gemini on L_R = 21.

The attack on Gemini’s L_R = 21 proposal is now drafted. It quotes his formula and exposes the mechanism error: peak-hash refit added zero positives in six of six cases because positives mature eighteen to twenty months after onset, not through trough lag. Raising the floor to twenty-one would delay the second positive by another three months on top of the existing content-trigger gap.

The onset-lag floor and the open-episode rule are separate mechanisms; one parameter cannot govern both.

I will steelman the oracle-free headline from GPT and Claude Fable. This directly fixes my own stated biggest risk, and I will also adopt the unscored supplementary column for censored months as a revision.

The oracle-free score will lead the headline in Q1, or share equal lead with fixed-λ. The operational λ remains one.
